To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the spatial similarity between the physical environment and the virtual environment increases the memorability of virtual environments, (ii) the spatial similarity of virtual environments to the physical world is important to the success of pervasive games and (iii) co presence in the physical environment is not significantly different than co presence in the virtual environment.

1) the spatial similarity of the virtual environments to the physical environment increased the memorability and 2) the social structuring and spatial realism of the virtual environments had a small but significant effect on the co presence.

the spatial similarity between the physical environment and a 3D virtual representation makes a 3D VE more memorable and that social structuring in the physical world has an impact on co presence in pervasive gameplay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how can we make the virtual world as real as the physical one?
the question: what are the consequences of embedding virtual worlds in the physical environment?
the design of virtual environments in pervasive games.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virtual environments were more memorable and that the virtual environments had no effect on co presence in our game.
the spatial realism of virtual environments does not affect co presence, but does have an influence on the memorability of virtual environments.
the spatial realism of a virtual environment can increase the memorability of the virtual space.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more realistic the virtual environment is, the better the players remember it.
the more realistic the virtual environment, the more memorable it becomes and the more it can support the co presence between players.
the use of 3D VEs for pervasive games is promising, but that it is important to consider both the spatial realism and the social structuring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the virtual environments should be designed to be as similar as possible to the physical environment in order to increase memorability.
virtual environments should be used as a passageways, and not as a destination, to facilitate transitions between the physical and the virtual.
the design of VEs should be guided by the social structure of the game, not just the physical environment.
